title: 2022 Fort St Legal Studies Trial
notes: Text extracted from the multiple-choice pages. No non-text figures were present in this section.

questions.stem: Federal Parliament passes a law banning the use of plastic bags. Which of the following human rights is being protected?

options.A: Environmental rights
options.B: Peace rights
options.C: Self-determination
options.D: Universal suffrage

questions.stem: Who bears the burden of proof in a criminal trial in the Supreme Court?

options.A: Magistrate
options.B: Judge
options.C: Jury
options.D: Director of Public Prosecution

questions.stem: Zeke receives a suspended sentence for committing a serious assault on Beth. Who would be most likely to appeal this decision?

options.A: Judge
options.B: Jury
options.C: Director of Public Prosecution
options.D: Public Defender

questions.stem: Which of the following purposes of punishment is achieved by diversionary programs?

options.A: Incapacitation
options.B: Retribution
options.C: Rehabilitation
options.D: Deterrence

questions.stem: Which of the following is an argument against entrenching a Charter of Rights in the Australian Constitution?

options.A: It could be easily amended by Parliament
options.B: It would promote a culture of respect for human rights in Australia
options.C: It may be expensive to introduce
options.D: It could never be amended

questions.answerNote: Entrenching needs a referendum, which is expensive; 'could never be amended' (D) overstates, since amendment is possible by referendum. A is an argument against a statutory charter, B is an argument for.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an aggravating factor in the sentencing of an offender?

options.A: The injury caused by the offence was not substantial
options.B: The victim provoked the offender
options.C: The offender has no record of previous convictions
options.D: The victim was elderly

questions.stem: Which of the following is a situational crime prevention strategy?

options.A: A local charity introduces a reading program for teenagers
options.B: A local council installs better lighting in a public park
options.C: A magistrate sentences an offender to imprisonment
options.D: A magistrate sentences an offender to a rehabilitation program

questions.stem: Richie is 10 years old. He assaults a person at a local shopping centre. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Richie has committed a public order offence
options.B: Richie cannot be found guilty of a crime
options.C: Richie can be found guilty of a crime
options.D: Richie has committed a strict liability offence

questions.answerNote: Changed from B. Ten is the age of criminal responsibility, so a 10 year old can be found guilty if the prosecution rebuts doli incapax.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a complete defence to an offence against the person?

options.A: Provocation
options.B: Excessive self defence
options.C: Substantial impairment by abnormality of the mind
options.D: Mental health impairment or cognitive impairment

questions.answerNote: Changed from C. Mental health impairment or cognitive impairment (Mental Health and Cognitive Impairment Forensic Provisions Act 2020) is a complete defence (not criminally liable); Provocation, excessive self-defence and substantial impairment are partial defences to murder.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the widespread or systematic murder of a civilian population?

options.A: Crimes against humanity
options.B: Aggression
options.C: Genocide
options.D: War crimes

questions.stem: Trinity has been charged with committing a serious indictable offence. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Trinity will be refused bail
options.B: Trinity may be refused bail
options.C: Trinity will be granted bail
options.D: Trinity cannot rely on self-defence as a complete defence to this charge

questions.stem: Which of the following best ensures the protection of human rights in Australia?

options.A: Ratification of an international human rights treaty
options.B: A media investigation into human rights abuses occurring in Australia
options.C: Enactment of Federal human rights legislation
options.D: An Australian non-government organisation offering support to victims of human rights abuses

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a role of a jury in a criminal trial?

options.A: To apply the law as directed by the judge
options.B: To decide whether the accused is guilty or not guilty
options.C: To attend the scene of the crime if directed by the judge
options.D: To participate in the sentencing process

questions.stem: Bree, who is 15 years old, has been charged with a summary offence. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Bree is not eligible to participate in a Youth Justice Conference
options.B: Bree may be eligible to participate in a Youth Justice Conference
options.C: Bree may be eligible to participate in Circle Sentencing
options.D: Bree may be eligible to participate in Forum Sentencing

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a post-sentencing consideration?

options.A: The security classification of the offender
options.B: The granting of parole to the offender
options.C: The validity of the offender’s visa
options.D: The aggravating and mitigating factors of the offender’s criminal actions

questions.stem: The Australian government decides to ignore a recommendation of the United Nations Human Rights Council. Which of the following concepts does this decision best reflect?

options.A: State sovereignty
options.B: Self-determination
options.C: Separation of powers
options.D: Division of power

questions.stem: Which of the following is part of the criminal investigation process?

options.A: Establishing a social crime prevention strategy
options.B: The arrest and detention of a suspect
options.C: Examining a range of factors that may lead to criminal behaviour
options.D: The allowance of the procedure of charge negotiation

questions.stem: Ben helps Di to plan a bank robbery. Di attempts to commit the bank robbery but is unsuccessful. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Ben has committed a preliminary crime; Di has committed a white-collar crime
options.B: Ben is an accessory before the fact; Di is an accessory after the fact
options.C: Ben and Di have both committed preliminary crimes
options.D: Ben and Di are both principals in the first degree

questions.answerNote: Ben (planning/conspiracy) and Di (attempt) have both committed preliminary crimes.

questions.stem: Raynor has been detained by police because it is suspected that he will commit a terrorist act next week. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Raynor does not have the right to contact a lawyer
options.B: Raynor is being held in protective custody
options.C: Raynor is being held in continued detention
options.D: Raynor is being held in preventative detention

questions.stem: Which of the following best represents the concept of the separation of powers protecting human rights?

options.A: The NSW State Parliament and the Federal Parliament both introduce anti- discrimination legislation on the same day
options.B: A District Court judge instructs a jury that they may deliver a majority verdict
options.C: The High Court rules that a piece of Federal legislation is constitutionally invalid
options.D: The NSW Court of Criminal Appeal issues a guideline judgement
